- File: tools/repo_tree/update_repo_tree.py
  Line or code reference: lines 179-181, in interaction with MARKER_PATTERN (line 19) and MARKER_COMMENT_HINT_PATTERN (line 22)
  Problem: parse_marker_spans strips only newline characters from each line (`raw_line.rstrip("\n")` + manual `\r` strip) but does not strip other trailing whitespace. When a valid marker line such as `<!-- TREE:START id=workflows -->  ` carries trailing spaces (common after editor reformatting or merge-tool artifacts), MARKER_PATTERN.fullmatch fails because the pattern ends with `-->` and fullmatch requires the entire string to match. The line then falls through to MARKER_COMMENT_HINT_PATTERN.fullmatch, which does match (its `\s*$` suffix absorbs the trailing spaces), and parse_marker_spans raises a RepoTreeError with exit_code=EXIT_MARKER_ERROR (2) for a "malformed TREE marker line".
  Why it fails at runtime: Running `make generate-check` (which calls `python3 tools/repo_tree/update_repo_tree.py --check`) on a repo whose agents.md has trailing whitespace after any marker line will produce a false-positive hard failure with exit code 2 and the message "malformed TREE marker line N: <!-- TREE:START id=workflows -->" instead of either accepting the valid marker or reporting ordinary drift as exit code 1.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5

A valid marker line like `<!-- TREE:START id=workflows -->   ` (with trailing spaces) fails fullmatch, falls through to the hint check (which also fails due to trailing whitespace), and is treated as regular prose content.
  Why it fails at runtime: If a user or merge tool adds trailing whitespace to a marker line in agents.md, `--check` could misclassify it as drift or miss that a marker pair exists at all.

A malformed marker like `<!--TREE:START id=.invalid-->` (no space after `TREE:START` or around `=`) bypasses the hint check and falls through as ordinary content instead of triggering the hard exit-2 failure.
  Why it fails at runtime: Malformed marker declarations with whitespace-edge cases silently degrade to drift (exit 1) instead of the contract-mandated hard failure (exit 2).
  SEVERITY: NIT

- File: tools/repo_tree/update_repo_tree.py

  Problem: The YAML error handling catches `yaml.YAMLError` but doesn't explicitly handle duplicate keys in the config file. PyYAML's `safe_load` silently overwrites duplicate keys with the last value, so a config like `marker_id: foo` followed by `marker_id: bar` would not raise an error.
  Why it fails at runtime: A user editing config.yaml who duplicates a key by mistake would get silent data loss rather than a clear error message.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4

## CORRECTNESS & LOGIC

File: tools/repo_tree/update_repo_tree.py
Line or code reference: lines 27-33 (MARKER_ID_TOKEN regex)
Problem: The MARKER_ID_TOKEN regex `r"[A-Za-z0-9_](?:[A-Za-z0-9_.-]*[A-Za-z0-9_])?"` allows consecutive dots and dashes (e.g., `foo--bar`, `foo..bar`) in marker IDs.
Why it fails at runtime: While the pattern requires start/end with alphanumeric/underscore, it permits `foo-_-bar` or `foo..bar` internally. If such IDs are used in config.yaml, they produce technically valid but malformed-looking identifiers in the rendered TREE blocks, which could cause confusion or downstream parsing issues if other tools expect stricter identifier formats.
SEVERITY: NIT
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3

File: tools/repo_tree/update_repo_tree.py
Line or code reference: line 22 (MARKER_COMMENT_HINT_PATTERN)
Problem: The narrowed regex `^\s*<!-- TREE:(START|END)\s+id\s*=.*-->\s*$` requires whitespace after `id` and before `=`, which creates inconsistency with MARKER_PATTERN that allows `id=value` without spaces.
Why it fails at runtime: A malformed line like `<!--TREE:START id=.invalid-->` (no spaces around `=`) would bypass the hint check and fall through as ordinary drift (exit 1) instead of the intended hard marker error (exit 2). This creates inconsistent behavior between the parser and the malformed-marker detector.
SEVERITY: NIT
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3

Why it fails at runtime: If config.yaml contains duplicate tree entries with the same marker_id, the last one wins silently instead of failing with a clear error. This could lead to confusing behavior where expected tree blocks are missing because one entry shadowed another.
